knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of a Tangent Line of a Curve at a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
Find $m,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=k(x)$ at the point where $x=0.$

We have $k(x)=-x^{3} -4 x + 6 e^{x}$ and $k^{\prime}(x)=-3 x^{2} + 6 e^{x} -4.$

$m=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have $k(x)=-x^{3} -4 x + 6 e^{x}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=0$ is equal to $k^{\prime}(0).$ The given derivative is

$$
k^{\prime}(x)=-3 x^{2} + 6 e^{x} -4.
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=0$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}k^{\prime}(0) & =-3 (0)^{2} + 6 e^{(0)} -4 \\ & =-4+0+6 \\ & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $2.$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{4} -5 x^{3} -6 x^{2} -\frac{1}{x}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=4$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(4).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2 x^{4} -5 x^{3} -6 x^{2} -\frac{1}{x}) \\ & =2\cdot4x^{3}-5\cdot3x^{2}-6\cdot2x+x^{-2} \\ & =8 x^{3} -15 x^{2} -12 x + \frac{1}{x^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=4$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(4) & =8 (4)^{3} -15 (4)^{2} -12 (4) + \frac{1}{(4)^{2}} \\ & =\frac{1}{16}-240-48+512 \\ & =224+\frac{1}{16} \\ & =\frac{3585}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=4$ is

$$
m=f^{\prime}(4)=\frac{3585}{16}.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=2 x^{7} -7 x^{5} -339 x$ at the point where $x=2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{7} -7 x^{5} -339 x.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=2$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(2).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2 x^{7} -7 x^{5} -339 x) \\ & =14 x^{6} -35 x^{4} -339.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(2) & =14 (2)^{6} -35 (2)^{4} -339 \\ & =-339-560+896 \\ & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $-3.$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{6} -4 x^{4} + 7 x^{2} -4.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=-2$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(-2).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2 x^{6} -4 x^{4} + 7 x^{2} -4) \\ & =12x^{5}-4(4x^{3})+7(2x)-0 \\ & =12 x^{5} -16 x^{3} + 14 x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=-2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(-2) & =12 (-2)^{5} -16 (-2)^{3} + 14 (-2) \\ & =128-384-28 \\ & =-284.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-2$ is

$$
m=f^{\prime}(-2)=-284.
$$
